title: Count Single Flips to Balance Parentheses
description: Given a string `s` of length `n` consisting of `'('` and `')'`, return the number of indices `i` (`0 <= i < n`) such that flipping `s[i]` (changing `'('` to `')'` or `')'` to `'('`) transforms `s` into a **valid balanced parentheses string**.
hints: Flipping one character changes the total balance by -2 (for '(' -> ')') or +2 (for ')' -> '('), so a valid flip can only exist when the initial total balance is +2 or -2.

Precompute prefix balance `pref[i]`, prefix minimum `prefMin[i]`, and suffix minimum `sufMin[i]`: flipping index `i` keeps every prefix non-negative iff `prefMin[i - 1] >= 0` and `sufMin[i] >= 2` (when total == +2) or `sufMin[i] >= -2` (when total == -2).

examples.explanation: Flipping index 1 produces "()()" and flipping index 2 produces "(())", giving 2 valid indices.
Flipping index 1 produces "(()())" and flipping index 2 produces "()(())", giving 2 valid indices.
Already balanced (total balance 0), so any single flip makes it unbalanced (0 valid indices).
